'''Jūnisho Jinja''' (十二所神社), also referred to as '''Jūnisha Jinja''' (十二社神社), '''Jūni Hashira Jinja''' (十二柱神社), or '''Jūni Tenjin Jinja''' (十二天神社), are {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines}} found throughout {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}. Some of these shrines are also called '''Jūnishō''' (十二社). 

These shrines can be categorized into two main types:
1. Shrines dedicated to local mountain deities called '''Jūni-sama''' (Twelve Lords), associated with ancient rituals and the customs of the "Twelve Lectures." These shrines are primarily found in mountainous areas of eastern Japan, especially in the northern {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|qid=Q132480|lt=Kantō region}} and {{ill|Kōshin'etsu region|ar|منطقة كوشينيتسو|ca|Kōshin'etsu|ckb|ناوچەی کۆشینێتسو|cs|Kóšinecu|eo|Kōŝin'ecu|es|Región de Kōshin'etsu|fa|منطقه کوشین‌اتسو|fi|Kōshin’etsu|fr|Région du Kōshin'etsu|hr|Kōshin'etsu|id|Wilayah Koshinetsu|ilo|Rehion ti Kōshin'etsu|it|Kōshin'etsu|ja|甲信越地方|ko|고신에쓰 지방|lt|Košinecu regionas|nl|Koshinetsu|pl|Region Kōshin’etsu|pt|Região de Koshinetsu|ru|Косинъэцу|sh|Kōshin'etsu|sk|Kóšinecu|sv|Koshinetsu|th|โคชินเอ็ตสึ|tl|Kōshin'etsu|tr|Kōshin'etsu|ur|کوشینیتسو علاقہ|vi|Kōshin'etsu|zh|甲信越地方|qid=Q398208|lt=Kōshin'etsu region}}. Research indicates that 65% of the 438 shrines named Jūnisho or Jūnisha enshrine {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|abstract|Q386563|az|Ooyamatsimu|de|Ōyamatsumi|fa|اویاماتسومی|fr|Ōyamatsumi|hr|O-Yama-Tsu-mi|ja|オオヤマツミ|ko|오야마쓰미노카미|mni|ꯑꯣꯌꯃꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|ru|Ооямацуми|simple|Ōyamatsumi|sv|Ōyamatsumi|tr|Ōyamatsumi|zh|大山津見|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi}} as their main deity.
2. Shrines that enshrine the {{ill|Kumano shrine|ja|熊野三山|pl|Kumano Sanzan|ru|Три храма Кумано|zh|熊野三山|qid=Q10403700|lt=Kumano Sanzan}} deities (known as {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Gongen}}). These were originally called '''Jūnisho Gongen-sha'''. During the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}, many of these shrines modified their enshrined deities to the "{{ill|Kamiyonanayo|ja|天神七代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heavenly Generations Seven|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神世七代|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3275893}}" and "{{ill|Five Generations of Earth Deities|ja|地神五代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthly Generations Five|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q18337308}}," or the "Twelve Gods of the Heavenly Generation."
